question: When a specific amount of external energy is supplied to a metal surface, the emitted electrons do not all possess the same kinetic energy; instead, they show a distribution of energies. What is the primary reason for this variation in kinetic energy?

options.A: The incident energy is not absorbed uniformly by all electrons
options.B: Electrons originating from deeper layers suffer collisions and lose energy before escaping
options.C: The work function of the metal varies continuously with time
options.D: Some electrons are heavier than others, requiring more energy to move
